source_text:
Ὅταν τοίνυν ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς εἰρημένοις ἐλεγχθέντες ἀπορήσωσιν, ἐπὶ τοὺς μάρτυρας καταφεύγειν πειρῶνται· λέγοντες πολλοὺς ἔχειν μάρτυρας, καὶ τοῦτο εἶναι τεκμηρίον πιστὸν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ παρ’ αὐτοῖς λεγομένου προφητικοῦ πνεύματος. τὸ δέ ἐστιν ἄρα ὡς ἔοικε παντὸς μᾶλλον οὐκ ἀληθές. καὶ γὰρ τῶν ἄλλων αἱρέσεων τινὲς, πλείστους ὅσους ἔχουσι μάρτυρας· καὶ οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο δήπου συγκαταθησόμεθα, οὐδὲ ἀλήθειαν ἔχειν αὐτοὺς ὁμολογήσομεν. καὶ πρῶτοί γε οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Μαρκίωνος αἱρέσεως Μαρκιωνισταὶ καλούμενοι, πλείστους ὅσους ἔχειν Χριστοῦ μάρτυρας λέγουσιν· ἀλλὰ τόν γε Χριστὸν αὐτὸν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν οὐχ’ ὁμολογοῦσι. καὶ μετὰ βραχέα τούτοις ἐπιφέρει λέγων·
Ὅθεν τοι καὶ ἐπειδὰν οἱ ἐπὶ τὸ τῆς κατὰ ἀλήθειαν πίστεως μαρτύριον κληθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τύχωσι μετά τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν Φρυγῶν αἱρέσεως λεγομένων μαρτύρων, διαφέρονταί τε πρὸς αὐτοὺς, καὶ μὴ κοινωνήσαντες αὐτοῖς τελειοῦνται, διὰ τὸ μὴ βούλεσθαι συγκαταθέσθαι τῷ διὰ Μοντανοῦ καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν πνεύματι. καὶ ὅτι τοῦτο ἀληθὲς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων χρόνων ἐν Ἀπαμείᾳ τῇ πρὸς Μαιάνδρῳ τυγχάνει γεγενημένον, ἐν τοῖς περὶ Γάϊον καὶ Ἀλέξανδρον ἀπὸ Εὐμενείας μαρτυρήσασι, πρόδηλον.
orientation: The author has just finished listing the earlier proofs against the Montanists and now turns to their claim that their many martyrs prove the power of their prophetic spirit.
pass_a_gloss: When therefore, having been refuted in all the things that have been said, they are at a loss, they try to take refuge in the martyrs, saying that they have many martyrs, and that this is a trustworthy proof of the power of the prophetic spirit that is spoken of among them. But this is, as it seems, more than anything not true. For also of the other heresies some have very many martyrs; and not because of this, surely, shall we assent, nor shall we confess that they have the truth. And first indeed those from the heresy of Marcion, called Marcionites, say that they have very many martyrs of Christ; but they do not confess Christ himself according to truth. And after a little he adds to these things, saying: Wherefore indeed also whenever those who have been called to the martyrdom of the faith according to truth from the church happen to be with some of those from the heresy of the Phrygians who are called martyrs, they are at variance with them, and not having had communion with them they are perfected, because they do not wish to assent to the spirit through Montanus and the women. And that this is true, and has happened also in our own times at Apamea near the Maeander, in the case of Gaius and Alexander from Eumeneia who bore witness, is clear.

choices.english: try to take refuge in the martyrs
choices.why: Keeps the verb of attempt explicit and the metaphor of flight as refuge, matching the author's rhetorical framing.
rejected: attempt to flee to the martyrs

choices.why: Renders the adjective as a quality of the proof, preserving the Montanist claim as the author reports it.

choices.english: not because of this, surely, shall we assent
choices.why: Keeps the particle δήπου as 'surely' and the future tense of the verb, preserving the author's ironic tone.
rejected: we will not for this reason agree

choices.term: τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτὸν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν οὐχ' ὁμολογοῦσι
choices.english: they do not confess Christ himself according to truth
choices.why: Preserves the emphatic 'himself' and the phrase 'according to truth' which the author uses as a technical contrast to the Montanist claim.
rejected: they do not truly confess Christ

choices.why: Renders the passive of τελειόω in its martyrological sense of completing one's witness through death, without adding 'as martyrs'.

choices.term: τῷ διὰ Μοντανοῦ καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν πνεύματι
choices.english: the spirit through Montanus and the women
choices.why: Keeps the prepositional phrase 'through Montanus and the women' as the channel of the spirit, matching the author's polemical description.
rejected: the spirit of Montanus and the women

pass_b_english: So when they have been refuted on all these points and find themselves at a loss, they try to take refuge in the martyrs. They say they have many martyrs, and that this is trustworthy proof of the power of the spirit they call prophetic. But this, as it seems, is anything but true. For some of the other heresies also have a great many martyrs, and surely we shall not assent because of this, nor shall we confess that they possess the truth. First of all, those from the heresy of Marcion, called Marcionites, say they have a great many martyrs of Christ, yet they do not confess Christ himself according to truth.
And after a little the same author adds to this, saying:

Therefore, whenever those called to martyrdom for the faith according to truth from the church happen to be together with some of the so-called martyrs from the heresy of the Phrygians, they are at variance with them, and they are perfected without having had communion with them, because they do not wish to assent to the spirit through Montanus and the women. And that this is true, and that it happened in our own times at Apamea on the Maeander in the case of Gaius and Alexander from Eumeneia, who bore witness, is clear.

problems.why: Same group called three different names; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Use 'Montanists/Cataphrygians' consistently; note 'followers of Miltiades' is error.

problems.quote: And after a little he adds to this, saying:
problems.why: Unclear who 'he' is; the author or his source?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'he' = the earlier anti-Montanist writer quoted above.

problems.quote: heresy of those called followers of Miltiades
problems.why: Same movement called by four different labels without explanation of equivalence.
problems.fix: Note at first mention that all terms refer to the Montanists.

problems.quote: And after a little he adds to this, saying:
problems.why: 'He' refers to the source author, not the treatise author, but the referent is unclear after a section break.
problems.fix: Replace 'he' with 'the same author' or the source's name.

edits.old: And after a little he adds to this, saying:
edits.new: And after a little the same author adds to this, saying:

fixed: The reported glossary problems about 'followers of Miltiades' and 'heresy of those called followers of Miltiades' do not appear in this section; the source text here uses 'τῆς τῶν Φρυγῶν αἱρέσεως' (the heresy of the Phrygians), which is rendered correctly as 'the heresy of the Phrygians'.

The speaker problem is real: 'he' is ambiguous after the section break. The source says 'ἐπιφέρει λέγων' (he adds, saying), referring to the earlier anti-Montanist writer quoted above. Changed 'he' to 'the same author' to clarify the referent.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'the same author' refers to the source author quoted earlier, kept the quotation as a separate paragraph, and preserved all claims and references exactly.
